title: Lists that edit like an outliner
steps: Open Lists tour. Lists are drawn with real bullets that change with depth, numbers in a right-aligned column, guides for each level, and long items that wrap under their own text. Put the cursor on an item: the line doesn't move. Its indent, bullet and number stay, numbers are always their text, and a bullet shows its `-` only while the cursor is on it. Bold, links and a task's box and dates show their markdown only where the cursor is.

On "Order seeds", press Tab (or Alt-Right): it moves under "Plan the garden"'s previous item, taking Tomatoes and Basil with it. Shift-Tab (or Alt-Left) brings it back out, after its parent, and the items after it stay where they were. In Vim, >> and << do the same, and the cursor stays on the line; > and < on a visual selection move every item selected, as a block.

Indent works as Workflowy's does: only under the item above, one level at a time. Tab on the first item of a list, or on an item that's already the first child, does nothing, and the status bar says why for a moment ("Can't indent: nothing above to nest under"). Select several items whose first can't indent, and none of them move. Off a list, Alt-Right and Alt-Left move by word, as usual.
Alt-Down (or ]e in Vim) on "Fix the bike" moves it below "Call the plumber", its patch with it; Alt-Up (or [e) moves it back.

In the numbered list, move "Fold in the butter" up: the numbers follow. Indent "Mix the dry things": it becomes 1. under Preheat, and the rest renumber. Delete a line: the numbers close up, in the same undo step.
At the end of an item, Enter starts the next one (a task starts a task, a number the next number). Enter again on the empty item steps out a level, then out of the list.
Click the bullet of "Plan the garden" (or za in Vim): its children fold away behind a …; the bullet gets a ring. Click again to bring them back.
⌘⇧P, Make a numbered list on the bullets, or Make tasks: the items change, their text and children stay.
Turn Lists off in the Extensions view and reload: lists are plain markdown, and Tab does nothing special.
